clauses.scope_note: Each Contributor grants a non-exclusive, worldwide, royalty-free copyright license in that Contributor’s Contribution and its Derivative Works, for a Non-competitive Purpose only. clauses.condition_explanation: non_competitive_purpose excludes providing others a product or service with the same or substantially similar functionality as SonarQube, competing with SonarQube, and engaging non-Program AI to ingest, interpret, analyze, train on, or interact with Program-provided data or otherwise engage with the Program.

clauses.scope_note: Each Contributor grants a non-exclusive, worldwide, royalty-free patent license under that Contributor’s Licensed Patents to make, use, sell, offer to sell, import, and otherwise transfer that Contributor’s Contribution, in Source Code or other form. A combination with the Program is covered only if, when the Contribution was added, that addition caused the combination to be covered by the Licensed Patents; no other combination is covered. The allowed activity labels approximate the enumerated patent rights; OfferPaidAccess captures offering to sell, not a separate general service grant.
clauses.condition_explanation: non_competitive_purpose has the exclusions stated in the definition at lines 52–57.

clauses.clause_label: 2(c) Recipient responsibility for other intellectual property rights
clauses.scope_note: As a condition of exercising the Agreement’s rights and licenses, the Recipient assumes sole responsibility to secure any other intellectual property rights needed. The text gives obtaining a required third-party patent license before distributing the Program as an example.
clauses.condition_explanation: secure_other_intellectual_property_rights_needed means obtaining any additional intellectual property rights actually needed; the clause does not assert that additional rights are always needed.

clauses.clause_label: 3.1 Contributor distribution: Source Code availability and information
clauses.scope_note: A Contributor distributing the Program in any form must also make the Program available as Source Code in accordance with section 3.2, accompany the Program with a statement that its Source Code is available under the Agreement, and inform Recipients how reasonably to obtain it on or through a customary software-exchange medium.
clauses.condition_explanation: The duties arise when a Contributor distributes the Program in any form. The required availability, statement, and obtaining instructions are cumulative.

clauses.clause_label: 3.2 Distribution of Program as Source Code
clauses.scope_note: When the Program is distributed as Source Code, it must be made available under this Agreement and each copy must include a copy of the Agreement.
clauses.condition_explanation: Both requirements apply when the Program is distributed as Source Code.

clauses.scope_note: A Contributor may not remove or alter Notices contained within the Program from any copy of the Program that it distributes. The Contributor may add its own appropriate Notices.
clauses.condition_explanation: The preservation duty applies to copies of the Program distributed by a Contributor; adding appropriate Notices is expressly allowed.

clauses.scope_note: If a Recipient institutes patent litigation against any entity alleging that the Program itself infringes the Recipient’s patents, that Recipient’s Section 2(b) patent rights terminate as of filing. Allegations about combinations of the Program with other software or hardware are excluded. This terminates the patent grant, not the separate copyright grant.
clauses.condition_explanation: recipient_institutes_patent_litigation means the Recipient files patent litigation, including a cross-claim or counterclaim. The allegation must concern the Program itself and not a combination with other software or hardware.

clauses.clause_label: 6 Termination for material noncompliance; cessation and survival
clauses.scope_note: All Recipient rights under the Agreement terminate if the Recipient fails to comply with a material term or condition and does not cure within a reasonable period after becoming aware of the noncompliance. Upon termination, the Recipient agrees to cease use and distribution of the Program as soon as reasonably practicable. The Recipient’s obligations and licenses it granted relating to the Program survive. The clause does not specify separate termination effects for rights in unrelated artifacts.
clauses.condition_explanation: material_noncompliance_not_cured means a failure to comply with a material term or condition that remains uncured for a reasonable period after the Recipient becomes aware of it.

coverage_notes: The supplied text is the SONAR Source-Available License v1.0, not evidence of a separate repository-specific license grant or of which Contributions are present. The grants cover only a Contributor’s Contribution and, where stated, its Derivative Works; no rights are inferred for third-party dependencies or unrelated artifacts.

The Non-competitive Purpose definition at lines 52–57 supplies the exclusions used for the conditional grants. Competitive use, substantially similar offerings to others, and the specified non-Program AI activities fall outside the grant; the text does not grant those activities.

Section 2(b) expressly gives patent rights to make, import, and otherwise transfer, but the allowed activity vocabulary has no exact labels for all of those acts. No additional software, hosting, network-service, training, or output rights are inferred.

Section 6 at lines 178–181 reserves rights not expressly granted; it does not create an independent blanket prohibition on activities involving unrelated artifacts. Warranty and liability disclaimers were omitted as not operative activity permissions, prohibitions, or obligations.
